Technology stocks were softer in Tuesday's pre-market, with the shares of tech stocks in the S&P 500 losing over 0.8% in value in the morning.
Among technology stocks moving on news:
(-) United Technologies ( UTX ) was slipping in Tuesday's pre-market, falling over 2%, after late Monday confirming plans to split into the three independent companies as it completed its $30 billion acquisition of Rockwell Collins. Moving ahead, the combination of Collins Aerospace Systems and UTX's defense and aerospace business will continue under the United Tech name while the new Pratt & Whitney, Otis, company will produce elevators and moving walkways. The third separate business, Carrier, will make heating, ventilation and air conditioning materials along with refrigeration and building automation products. The three-way split is expected to be completed in 2020.
In other sector news:
(-) Apple ( AAPL ) was down about 1.6% in early Tuesday trading after analysts at RBC Capital Markets lowered their price target for the tech giant by $5 to $235 a share and also trimmed its lowered its earnings and revenue estimates for the next few quarters, citing "recent data points related to iPhone demand."
(-) B.O.S. Better Online Solutions ( BOSC ) fell about 2% in late trading Monday night despite reporting big jumps in Q3 net income and revenue over year-ago levels. Net income for the three months ended Sept. 30 increased 63.6% year over year to $216,000, or $0.06 per share, compared with a $132 million, or $0.04 per share, profit for the Israeli radio frequency identification company last year. Revenue rose 6.7% over the same quarter last year to $7.7 million from $7.2 million last year. Analyst estimates were not available for comparison.
